subject: Availability commitments and monthly remedy for Greenline
messages:
From: Sam Green <sam.green@greenline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Availability commitment and monthly remedy - Greenline / Redwood

Karthik —

Thanks for the draft SLA. A couple of things floated up from our ops and procurement teams after the initial read:

1) For our batched inference workloads (nightly scoring jobs), we need a carveout or a lower baseline. Those jobs can tolerate higher latency and occasional short blips, but the current 99.95% uptime baseline and corresponding credit model blows past our internal cost tolerances.

2) We want clarity on how scheduled maintenance (weekly patch windows) and cold-cache warmup penalties are handled — specifically whether degradation during a cache-warm period counts toward uptime.

3) Monthly credit cap: we’d prefer a lower absolute cap (10% of monthly invoice) with a pro-rata calculation per impacted day, rather than a large uncapped percent.

I attached a marked-up copy of the SLA draft with comments (Greenline_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf). Can Redwood propose a pragmatic path that preserves production guarantees for latency-sensitive API traffic while recognizing differences for batch workloads?

Sam
Sam Green
Head of Platform Engineering | Greenline Systems

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability commitment and monthly remedy - Greenline / Redwood

Sam —

Appreciate the detailed read and the markup. High level response: Redwood is happy to separate guarantees by workload class. Proposal outline attached (redwood-sla-matrix.xlsx) but here are the key points so we can iterate quickly:

- Hosted (API text/chat): keep standard 99.95% monthly availability. Credits: scaling ladder with a monthly cap equal to 20% of monthly invoice.
- Dedicated / Batch (nightly scoring, large-batch jobs): we can offer a lower baseline of 99.5% availability, with a smaller credit ladder and a monthly cap at 15% of that portion of the bill.
- Scheduled maintenance: 4 hours/week maintenance windows per region are excluded from uptime calculations if announced 7 days in advance. Emergency maintenance will be handled case-by-case and may be excluded for critical security patches.
- Cache warmup: we propose a 15-minute warmup exclusion per instance restart; beyond that, degradation counts toward uptime.

If acceptable, Laura can take a pass on contract language and we can return a marked-up SLA. I’ve attached a simple matrix to make tradeoffs visible.

Next steps: Laura / Marissa — can you suggest language for the monthly cap and pro-rata formula so Sam’s procurement team can route it?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Availability commitment and monthly remedy - Greenline / Redwood

Sam / Karthik —

Thanks — I took a contract-first pass and attached a redline (SLA_amendment_markup.docx). A few items I want to call out so we have alignment before legal finalizes:

1) Workload split: Redwood proposes a two-tier guarantee in contract language — Tier A (latency-sensitive hosted API): 99.95% monthly uptime; Tier B (batch/dedicated capacity): 99.5% monthly uptime. We will include explicit examples so there’s no ambiguity about which workloads fall into Tier B.

2) Remedy calculation: credits calculated pro-rata by the number of affected days in the month and applied only to the invoice line for the affected product (i.e., batch credits don’t reduce hosted API charges).

3) Monthly cap: we are willing to move the cap to 20% of the monthly invoice for aggregate credits (across products) or 15% if Greenline prefers caps per-product. Given the scale of the workloads you described, a 10% overall cap is tight — it would leave us insufficient runway to remediate persistent issues.

4) Burst / warmup: propose a 30-minute warmup exclusion for consecutive instance restarts caused by scaling events. We will instrument warmup more precisely and provide warmup metrics during the trial period.

If Greenline agrees in principle to the tiering and cap structure, we’ll produce a DocuSign-ready amendment for signature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Availability commitment and monthly remedy - Greenline / Redwood

Laura —

Thanks for the clear draft. We’re aligned on the two-tier approach; that addresses most of our operational concerns. A couple of asks from procurement:

- Can you confirm the per-product cap option formally (15% per product) and share a short example calculation? Procurement prefers per-product ceilings to avoid credits eating into unrelated spending lines.
- Given our nightly jobs can be noisy, we want the warmup exclusion window reduced to 20 minutes if internal instrumentation shows warmup is typically below that. Can Redwood commit to sharing warmup telemetry for the pilot?
- Finally, we’d like the monthly cap to be applied after calculating pro-rata credits, not before, so we can validate the math.

If you could produce the per-product example and update the redline, procurement will route internally and (hopefully) get sign-off this week.

Sam

Sam —

Great — glad we’re converging. Summary of agreed path and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Guarantees by workload class
   - Tier A (hosted API / latency sensitive): 99.95% monthly availability.
   - Tier B (dedicated / batch): 99.5% monthly availability.

2) Warmup exclusion
   - Agreed to 20 minutes warmup exclusion for the pilot; Redwood will provide warmup telemetry (per-instance warmup time and warmup start events) for the first 60 days.

3) Remedy calculation and cap
   - Credits are calculated pro-rata by the number of affected days and applied to the invoice line for the affected product.
   - Per-product monthly cap: 15% of that product line item. After calculating pro-rata credits we then apply the per-product cap (i.e., cap is applied to the credit amount, not to the baseline bill). Example: if batch line is $50k/month and pro-rata credits sum to $9k, cap at 15% would allow up to $7.5k; Redwood pays $7.5k.

4) Next steps
   - I’ll upload a DocuSign-ready amendment reflecting the per-product cap and warmup telemetry obligation (link below). Laura will send the final redline for your review.
